facts.statement: In 2010, a team led by Federico Gianechini cast doubt on the claim that Sinornithosaurus was venomous.

facts.statement: Sinornithosaurus belonged to the family Dromaeosauridae, a group of agile predators known for having a distinctive sickle-shaped claw on their toes.
facts.quote: Sinornithosaurus was a member of the family Dromaeosauridae, a group of agile, predatory dinosaurs with a distinctive sickle-shaped toe claw, which also includes Deinonychus and Utahraptor.

facts.statement: Sinornithosaurus millenii lived approximately 125 million years ago during the Barremian age of the Early Cretaceous, making it one of the earliest known dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: S. millenii lived about 125 million years ago in the Barremian age of the Early Cretaceous period, which makes it among the earliest and most primitive dromaeosaurids yet discovered.

facts.statement: Fossils of Sinornithosaurus haoiana and the specimen NGMC 91 date to approximately 122 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils of S. haoiana and the possible Sinornithosaurus specimen NGMC 91 were found in younger strata dating to about 122 million years ago.

facts.statement: The type species Sinornithosaurus millenii was described in 1999.
facts.quote: S. millenii ("millennium Chinese bird-lizard") is the type species, described in 1999.

facts.statement: A second species, Sinornithosaurus haoiana, was described in 2004 based on a new specimen that differed from S. millenii in skull and hip features.
facts.quote: A second species, S. haoiana ("Hao's Chinese bird-lizard") was described by Liu et al. in 2004 based on a new specimen, D2140, which differed from S. millenii in features of the skull and hips.

facts.statement: Turner, Makovicky, and Norell (2012) argued that the distinguishing features of S. haoiana were either present in S. millenii or variable, leading them to consider S. haoiana a junior synonym of S. millenii.
facts.quote: However, according to Turner, Makovicky and Norell (2012) the supposed distinguishing features of S. haoiana "are either present in Sinornithosaurus millenii or variable among the number of Sinornithosaurus specimens"; the authors considered S. haoiana to be a junior synonym of S. millenii.

facts.statement: The well-preserved specimen NGMC 91, nicknamed "Dave", was first described in a 2001 paper published in the journal Nature by Ji Qiang and colleagues.
facts.quote: An incredibly well-preserved microraptorian nicknamed "Dave" (specimen NGMC 91), was first described in a paper published in the journal Nature by Ji Qiang and colleagues in 2001.

facts.statement: A 2004 phylogenetic analysis by Phil Senter and colleagues found that specimen NGMC 91 was more closely related to Microraptor than to Sinornithosaurus millenii.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic studies did not support the idea that NGMC 91 was a close relative of S. millenii. In a 2004 analysis, Phil Senter and colleagues found that it was, in fact, more closely related to Microraptor.

facts.statement: In 2011, Phil Senter concluded that his earlier separation of NGMC 91 from S. millenii was based on anatomical misinterpretations after personally examining the holotype.
facts.quote: However, in a 2011 publication Senter stated that a personal examination of the holotype of S. millenii led him to conclude that his earlier separation of NGMC 91 from S. millenii was based on anatomical misinterpretations.

facts.statement: Turner, Makovicky, and Norell concluded that specimen NGMC 91 was a subadult individual of Sinornithosaurus millenii.
facts.quote: The authors concluded that NGMC 91 was a subadult specimen of S. millenii.

facts.statement: Sinornithosaurus was discovered by Xu Xing, Wang Xiaolin, and Wu Xiaochun of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology of Beijing.
facts.quote: Sinornithosaurus was discovered by Xu Xing, Wang Xiaolin and Wu Xiaochun of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology of Beijing.

facts.statement: An almost-complete fossil of Sinornithosaurus with feather impressions was recovered from the Yixian Formation in Liaoning Province, China, a site also known for four other feathered dinosaurs.
facts.quote: An almost-complete fossil with feather impressions, was recovered from Liaoning Province, China, in the Yixian Formation; the same incredibly rich location where four dinosaurs with feathers were discovered previously, Protarchaeopteryx, Sinosauropteryx, Caudipteryx, and Beipiaosaurus.

facts.statement: Sinornithosaurus holds the distinction of being the first dromaeosaurid dinosaur discovered with feathers.
facts.quote: Sinornithosaurus was the first dromaeosaurid discovered with feathers.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Sinornithosaurus, IVPP V12811, is housed in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, China.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is IVPP V12811, in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, China.

facts.statement: Specimen NGMC 91 is held in the National Geological Museum of China and was collected from the Fanzhangzi quarry near Lingyuan City, Liaoning Province.
facts.quote: The NGMC 91 specimen is in the collection of the National Geological Museum of China. It was collected in Fanzhangzi quarry, near Lingyuan City, Liaoning Province.

facts.statement: The discovery of Sinornithosaurus millenii in 1999 caused a sensation because it was the fifth non-avian dinosaur with feathers to be discovered.
facts.quote: Cuando se encontró la primera especie, Sinornithosaurus millenii, en 1999 causó gran sensación porque era el quinto dinosaurio no aviar con plumas descubierto.

facts.statement: The first species, Sinornithosaurus millenii, was collected from the Sihetun site in western Liaoning.
facts.quote: Fue recogido del sitio de Sihetun en Liaoning occidental.

facts.statement: Sinornithosaurus was among the smallest dromaeosaurids, with a length of about 90 centimeters.
facts.quote: Sinornithosaurus estaba entre los dromeosáuridos más pequeños, con una longitud de unos 90 centímetros.

facts.statement: Sinornithosaurus had proportionally very long arms and hands.
facts.quote: Sus brazos y manos eran proporcionalmente muy largos.

facts.statement: The presence of feathers in Sinornithosaurus suggests that other running dromaeosaurids, such as Velociraptor, may also have possessed feathers.
facts.quote: Sinornithosaurus sugiere que otros dromeosáuridos corredores, como el Velociraptor, también pudieron haber poseído plumas.

facts.statement: Sinornithosaurus was discovered by Xu Xing, Wang Xiaolin, and Wu Xiaochun of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
facts.quote: Sinornithosaurus fue descubierto por Xu Xing, Wang Xiaolin y Wu Xiaochun del Instituto de Paleontología de Vertebrados y Paleoantropología de Pekín.

facts.statement: A nearly complete fossil with feather impressions was recovered from the Yixian Formation in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: Un casi completo fósil con impresiones de plumas, recobrado de la Provincia de Liaoning, China, en la Formación Yixian.

facts.statement: Two species have been described: Sinornithosaurus millenii in 1999 and Sinornithosaurus haoiana in 2004.
facts.quote: Se han descrito dos especies: Sinornithosaurus millenii en el año 1999 y Sinornithosaurus haoiana en el 2004.

facts.statement: A small fossil specimen, likely a juvenile, identified as NGMC 91, has been nicknamed "Dave".
facts.quote: Este fósil, probablemente una cría, se identifica como NGMC 91, y ha sido apodado "Dave".

facts.statement: The holotype IVPP V12811 is held in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, China.
facts.quote: El holotipo IVPP V12811, se encuentra en la colección del Instituto de Paleontología de Vertebrados y Paleoantroplogía en Pekín, China.

facts.statement: In 2009, a team led by Enpu Gong examined a well-preserved skull and found evidence suggesting it is the first identified venomous dinosaur.
facts.quote: En 2009, un equipo de científicos liderado por Enpu Gong examinó un cráneo bien conservado de Sinornithosaurus y encontró evidencias que sugerían que se trata del primer dinosaurio venenoso identificado.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Sinornithosaurus may have specialized in hunting small prey, such as birds, similar to how snakes do today.
facts.quote: Gong et al. sugieren que Sinornithosaurus podría haberse especializado en cazar presas pequeñas, por ejemplo pájaros, como hacen las serpientes actualmente.

facts.statement: Sinornithosaurus lived 125 million years ago during the Barremian (Early Cretaceous), making it one of the oldest and most primitive members of its family.
facts.quote: Sinornithosaurus vivió hace 125 millones de años en el Barremiense (Cretácico Inferior), lo que lo hace uno de los más antiguos y primitivos miembros de esta familia.

facts.statement: Xu Xing described Sinornithosaurus and presented a phylogenetic analysis demonstrating it is a basal, or primitive, dromaeosaurid.
facts.quote: Xu Xing describe a Sinornithosaurus y presenta un análisis filogenético en el que demuestran que se trata de un basal, o primitivo, dromeosáurido.

facts.statement: A second species, S. haoiana, meaning "Chinese Hao bird-lizard", was described by Liu et al. in 2004 based on a specimen differing from S. millenii in head and hip characters.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie S. haoiana, "lagarto ave chino de Hao ", fue descrita por Liu et al. en 2004 basándose en un espécimen que difiere de S. millenii en caracteres de la cabeza y cadera.

facts.statement: However, Turner, Makovicky, and Norell in 2012 argued that the supposed distinctive features of S. haoiana are present in S. millenii or vary among Sinornithosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, según Turner, Makovicky y Norell en 2012, las supuestas características distintivas de S. haoiana "están presentes en Sinornithosaurus millenii o son variables entre el número de especímenes de Sinornithosaurus ".

facts.statement: The authors considered S. haoiana to be a junior synonym of S. millenii.
facts.quote: Los autores consideraron S. haoiana como un sinónimo menor de S. millenii.

facts.statement: Researchers initially refused to name the specimen because, although fully articulated, almost all bones broke when the fossil slabs were split, leaving only clear silhouettes of the bones.
facts.quote: Se negaron a nombrar el espécimen porque, aunque está completamente articulado, casi todos los huesos se rompieron cuando se partieron las losas fósiles, por lo que solo las siluetas de estos huesos son claras en la mayor parte de la parte y la contraparte.

facts.statement: Stephen Czerkas and colleagues considered the specimen to represent their newly described species Cryptovolans pauli, now generally considered a synonym of Microraptor gui, based on alleged wing proportions.
facts.quote: Stephen Czerkas y sus colegas consideraron que el espécimen representaba un ejemplo de su especie recién descrita Cryptovolans pauli, ahora generalmente considerada un sinónimo de Microraptor gui, basándose en las supuestas proporciones de las alas.

facts.statement: In a 2004 analysis, Phil Senter and colleagues found that the specimen was actually more closely related to Microraptor.
facts.quote: En un análisis de 2004, Phil Senter y sus colegas encontraron que, de hecho, estaba más estrechamente relacionado con Microraptor.

facts.statement: However, in a 2011 publication, Senter declared that a personal examination of the S. millenii holotype led him to conclude his previous separation of NGMC 91 from S. millenii was based on erroneous anatomical interpretations.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en una publicación de 2011, Senter declaró que un examen personal del holotipo de S. millenii lo llevó a concluir que su separación anterior de NGMC 91 de S. millenii se basó en interpretaciones anatómicas erróneas.

facts.statement: Because the two specimens were "identical in all character states" used in his phylogenetic analysis, were from similar stratigraphic levels, and "uniquely shared the presence of a triangular coracoid with a large oval foramen", Senter concluded NGMC 91 belongs to the species Sinornithosaurus millenii.
facts.quote: Como los dos especímenes eran "idénticos en todos los estados de caracteres" utilizados en su análisis filogenético, eran de niveles estratigráficos similares y "compartían de forma única la presencia de una coracoides triangular con un gran foramen ovalado", Senter concluyó que NGMC 91 pertenece a la especie Sinornithosaurus millenii.

facts.statement: Turner, Makovicky, and Norell, in 2012, also reached the same conclusion independently of Senter.
facts.quote: Turner, Makovicky y Norell, en 2012, también llegaron a la misma conclusión independientemente de Senter.

facts.statement: On the other hand, it possesses a posteriorly bifurcated dentary, which is an apomorphy of Sinornithosaurus.
facts.quote: Por otro lado, posee un dentario bifurcado posteriormente, que es una apomorfia de Sinornithosaurus.

facts.statement: The authors concluded that NGMC 91 was a subadult specimen of S. millenii.
facts.quote: Los autores concluyeron que NGMC 91 era un espécimen subadulto de S. millenii.

facts.statement: The body feathers of Sinornithosaurus measured generally between 3 to 4.5 centimeters and were composed of filaments showing characteristics of early feathers.
facts.quote: Las plumas corporales medían generalmente entre 3 a 4,5 centímetros, estaban compuestas de filamentos, y mostraron dos características que indican que son plumas tempranas.

facts.statement: According to NGMC - 91, feathers covered the entire body of Sinornithosaurus, including the head in front of the eyes, neck, arms, long feathers on the thighs, and a tail like that of Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: En NGMC - 91 las plumas cubrieron el cuerpo entero, incluyendo la cabeza por delante de los ojos, el cuello, brazos, plumas largas en los muslos, y una la cola como la de Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: A 2010 study indicated that Sinornithosaurus may have had feathers that varied significantly in color across different body zones, based on microscopic cellular structure analysis of preserved fossils.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2010 indicó que Sinornithosaurus puede haber tenido plumas que variaban en color significativamente a través de distintas zonas del cuerpo, basándose en análisis de estructuras celulares microscópicas en los fósiles preservadas.

facts.statement: A subsequent 2012 study showed that the colors of Sinornithosaurus were reddish-brown, yellow, black, and gray, which were scattered across its body.
facts.quote: Un estudio posterior de 2012 mostró que los colores de Sinornithosaurus eran pardo-rojizo, amarillo, negro y gris, los cuales estaban dispersos por su cuerpo.

facts.statement: In 2009, a team led by Empu Gong examined a well-preserved Sinornithosaurus skull and noted features suggesting it was the first identified poisonous dinosaur.
facts.quote: En 2009, un equipo de científicos dirigido por Empu Gong examinó un cráneo de Sinornithosaurus bien conservado y notó varias características que sugerían que era el primer dinosaurio venenoso identificado.

facts.statement: However, in 2010, a team led by Federico Gianechini published an article questioning the claim that Sinornithosaurus was poisonous.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2010, otro equipo de científicos dirigido por Federico Gianechini publicó un artículo que ponía en duda la afirmación de que Sinornithosaurus era venenoso.

facts.statement: Gong and colleagues suggested that unique features indicated Sinornithosaurus may have specialized in hunting small prey like birds, using long fangs to penetrate feathers and poison/paralyze prey like a modern snake.
facts.quote: Gong y sus colegas sugirieron que estas características únicas indicaban que Sinornithosaurus puede haberse especializado en cazar presas pequeñas como aves, usando sus largos colmillos para penetrar las plumas y envenenar y aturdir a la presa, como una serpiente moderna.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that grooved teeth are not exclusive to this genus and are found in many other theropods, including other dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Señalaron que los dientes ranurados no son exclusivos de este género y, de hecho, los dientes ranurados se encuentran en muchos otros terópodos, incluidos otros dromeosáuridos.

facts.statement: Finally, researchers could not independently verify the presence of supposed venom gland chambers cited by Gong's team, finding only normal cranial sinuses.
facts.quote: Finalmente, no pudieron verificar de forma independiente la presencia de supuestas cámaras para las glándulas venenosas citadas por el equipo de Gong, encontrando solo los senos normales del cráneo.

facts.statement: Gong's team presented a new evaluation questioning their 2010 findings, admitting grooved teeth were common among theropods but suggesting they prevailed only among feathered maniraptorans, and hypothesizing that venom may have been a primitive trait for all archosaurs or reptiles maintained in certain lineages.
facts.quote: Gong y su equipo presentaron una nueva evaluación del estudio de 2010, poniendo en duda sus hallazgos. Admitieron que los dientes acanalados eran comunes entre los terópodos, aunque sugirieron que en realidad solo prevalecían entre los maniraptoranos emplumados, y plantearon la hipótesis de que el veneno puede haber sido un rasgo primitivo para todos los arcosaurios, si no para todos los reptiles, que se mantuvo en ciertos linajes.
